overview: The file brings together 1948–1949 correspondence concerning a proposed American Press Institute program, potentially financed by the Rockefeller Foundation, through which selected Japanese publishers and editors would study the press and public affairs in the United States during the Allied occupation of Japan. The writers debate participant selection, program length, regional placements, press freedom, labor relations, political reporting, objectivity, and the potentially disruptive effects of exposing Japanese journalists to aggressive American reporting techniques. Multiple State Department drafts and copies document official endorsement and coordination with the Department of the Army and SCAP. A second group of papers concerns Tokyo Asahi assistant foreign editor Isami Suzukawa’s 1949 visit to Washington and interview with George F. Kennan, arranged through personal introductions from New York Times journalists Lindesay Parrott and Arthur Krock.

subfiles.title: Taylor asks Saltzman for advice on a Japanese journalists’ program
subfiles.to: Charles E. Saltzman, Assistant Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Taylor forwards background correspondence and requests State Department advice concerning a proposed American program for Japanese publishers and editors.
subfiles.summary: Taylor asks whether Tokyo authorities accept the risks of teaching Japanese journalists aggressive US reporting methods.

subfiles.title: Taylor requests Army guidance on the Japanese press project
subfiles.to: Brigadier General George Eberle, Civil Affairs Division
subfiles.about: Taylor asks whether the Civil Affairs Division supports a Rockefeller-funded American study program for Japanese publishers and editors.
subfiles.summary: Taylor seeks Army assurance on a Japanese-journalist exchange program, asking about curriculum, participant numbers, and comparison to an earlier German program.

subfiles.title: Fahs advises Taylor on the design of a Japanese journalists’ exchange
subfiles.about: Fahs analyzes the Japanese press and proposes the composition, duration, and curriculum of a U.S. visit by six Japanese journalists.
subfiles.summary: Fahs recommends a substantive exchange for six diverse Japanese journalists addressing press ownership, labor, and criticism, with a long US stay and no public statements.

subfiles.title: Taylor seeks Nugent’s reaction to an exploratory exchange proposal
subfiles.to: Colonel Donald Nugent, CIE Section, GHQ, SCAP
subfiles.about: Taylor asks Nugent whether a carefully prepared American program for Japanese editors would serve U.S. policy in occupied Japan.
subfiles.summary: Taylor describes preliminary funding talks and asks Nugent's reaction to the Japanese journalist-exchange proposal.

subfiles.title: Early State Department draft endorsing the press program
subfiles.from: Frank A. Schuler Jr., Department of State
subfiles.about: A draft State Department response endorses the Japanese journalists’ visit and recommends a six-month emphasis on responsible and objective reporting.
subfiles.summary: Draft endorses the journalists' program, proposing young participants and topics like labor, democracy, and the Atlantic Pact.

subfiles.title: First page of expanded McNally draft reply to Taylor
subfiles.from: John H. McNally, Department of State (identified from the continuation on page 13)
subfiles.about: This expanded draft gives detailed State Department recommendations for the proposed program and criticizes prewar Japanese journalism.
subfiles.summary: Draft recommends young, change-receptive Japanese journalists for a six-month exchange on responsible, objective reporting.

subfiles.title: Cleared State Department draft reply to Taylor
subfiles.from: Frank A. Schuler Jr., Department of State
subfiles.about: A cleared draft conveys official State Department support and curricular recommendations for the Japanese journalists’ program.
subfiles.summary: Cleared State draft backs the exchange for young journalists on a six-month US stay studying objective reporting.

subfiles.title: Information copy of Taylor’s reply to Schuler
subfiles.to: Frank A. Schuler Jr., Department of State
subfiles.about: Taylor thanks Schuler for official encouragement and agrees to proceed with tentative planning if SCAP responds favorably.
subfiles.summary: Taylor tells Schuler the Japanese program must differ from the earlier, more basic German-journalist program.

subfiles.title: File copy of Taylor’s reply to Schuler
subfiles.to: Frank A. Schuler Jr., Department of State
subfiles.about: A stamped file copy preserves Taylor’s acknowledgment of State Department support for the proposed program.
subfiles.summary: File copy repeats Taylor's point that Japan's advanced press needs a program unlike the German one.

subfiles.title: Department of State reference slip
subfiles.about: A brief internal routing slip carries a fragmentary handwritten instruction concerning preparation or action by another person.
subfiles.summary: Reference slip's routing marks are illegible, with only a garbled handwritten fragment remaining.

subfiles.title: Closing page of McNally draft reply
subfiles.from: John H. McNally, Department of State
subfiles.about: A badly degraded closing fragment appears to complete the expanded State Department draft begun on page 8.
subfiles.summary: Closing fragment of a draft letter recommends further consultation, signed by McNally with Schuler's drafting initials.

subfiles.title: Parrott introduces Isami Suzukawa to Kennan
subfiles.from: Lindesay Parrott, The New York Times
subfiles.to: George F. Kennan, Department of State
subfiles.about: Parrott introduces Tokyo Asahi assistant foreign editor Isami Suzukawa and asks Kennan to provide him with background information.
subfiles.summary: Parrott introduces visiting Japanese journalist Suzukawa to Kennan, suggesting background briefing rather than interview.

subfiles.title: Parrott thanks Kennan for meeting Suzukawa
subfiles.from: Lindesay Parrott, The New York Times
subfiles.to: George F. Kennan, Department of State
subfiles.about: Parrott thanks Kennan for receiving Suzukawa and comments on the journalist’s reporting and Japanese views of the prospective peace treaty.
subfiles.summary: Parrott thanks Kennan for meeting journalist Suzukawa, praising his accurate and even-handed reporting.

subfiles.title: Krock recommends that Kennan see Suzukawa
subfiles.about: Krock sends Kennan a short personal recommendation that he meet Isami Suzukawa if his schedule permits.
subfiles.summary: Krock's brief note recommends Kennan meet visiting journalist Suzukawa.

subfiles.title: Kennan reports on his meeting with Suzukawa
subfiles.about: Kennan tells Parrott that Suzukawa concentrated on interviewing him rather than discussing impressions from his European trip.
subfiles.summary: Kennan reports Suzukawa was too intent on questioning him to share his own impressions of Europe.

interest: Shows postwar US efforts to train Japanese journalists, weighing benefits against fears of overly aggressive reporting.
